_why: D-P10-92w asked for a stated-once check. Three claims had each been corrected in one place and left wrong in another, and my reply then asserted the correction was complete. A canonical sentence plus a list of superseded wordings makes that failure mechanical to detect instead of relying on me having looked everywhere.
_how: python3 check_claims.py  — exits 1 if any released text carries a superseded wording. Run it before any release commit.

claims.canonical: LABEL_ONLY matches any line of letters and spaces, so it skips a short punctuation-free prose line as well as a markdown label; bullets and lines containing punctuation are not skipped.
The registration states the halt rule twice and differently; we adopted the per-arm reading and record both wordings at D-15.
superseded: THE HALT RULE. A PC-4 failure halts
The registered rule halted their temperature-0 arms,
registered rule halted the temperature-0 arm and

claims.canonical: hydrate_faireval.py verifies an existing checkout against pinned hashes and byte lengths. It does not fetch.
superseded: inputs are fetched at run time

scope.exempt_note: DEVIATIONS.md may quote a superseded wording INSIDE a dated entry that records the correction. Such a quote must appear within 400 characters of the word 'superseded', 'was FALSE', 'earlier wording' or 'we quoted only one side'; the checker enforces that rather than exempting the file.
